claim.why_it_matters: Same internal inconsistency as 11.9.6: FLOAT-BINARY and FLOAT-DECIMAL are lifted out of '## 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph' and become its peers, so a depth-based outline or TOC no longer shows them as clauses of the OPTIONS paragraph.

verdict.reasoning: Independently verified against a fresh 300 dpi render of PDF page 305 (printed page 275) and, for the peer comparison, page 302 (printed 272). PDF p.305 prints, in order: '11.9.8  FLOAT-BINARY clause', '11.9.8.1 General', '11.9.8.2 General format', '11.9.8.3 Syntax rules', '11.9.9  FLOAT-DECIMAL clause', '11.9.9.1 General', '11.9.9.2 General format'. PDF p.302 prints '11.9  OPTIONS paragraph', '11.9.1 General' ... '11.9.5  ARITHMETIC clause', '11.9.5.1 General format'. So 11.9.8 and 11.9.9 are three-component (sub-subclause) numbers under 11.9, exactly the same depth as 11.9.5 -- confirmed by the printed dotted numbering, and by the p.302 general format which lists float-binary-clause and float-decimal-clause as clauses OF the OPTIONS paragraph. The markdown transcription is quoted correctly: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13142 '## 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph', :13175 '### 11.9.5 ARITHMETIC clause' with children at '####' (:13180, :13191), but :13308 '## 11.9.8 FLOAT-BINARY clause' and :13336 '## 11.9.9 FLOAT-DECIMAL clause' with children at '###' (:13311, :13316, :13327, :13339, :13344). The per-page slice E:/Temp/specrecon/v305/page-305.md agrees. Nothing is textually missing -- all heading text, both general formats and all three FLOAT-BINARY syntax rules are present, and the figure notes correctly record the FLOAT-DECIMAL choice indicators. The defect is purely one of heading DEPTH, but that depth is not cosmetic: it asserts a different parentage than the printed standard, making FLOAT-BINARY/FLOAT-DECIMAL siblings of 11.9 rather than its clauses, so any depth-derived outline, TOC or chunker mis-parents them. Rejection criteria checked and none apply: text is not missing/reflowed, this is not page-break furniture or wrapping, and the claim misquotes neither source. One nuance that does NOT defeat the claim: ISO's own typography uses one bold weight and essentially one size for every heading level (verified by comparing '11.9', '11.9.5' and '11.9.5.1' on p.302), so 'same weight and size as 11.9.5' is true but carries no information -- the printed depth signal is the dotted number, not the type size.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and the claim understates the scope. Confirmed on page 305: '## 11.9.8 FLOAT-BINARY clause' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13308) and '## 11.9.9 FLOAT-DECIMAL clause' (:13336) are transcribed at heading level 2, the same level as their parent '## 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph' (:13142), whereas the peer sub-subclause 11.9.5 ARITHMETIC clause is correctly at level 3 (:13175). Two refinements: (1) the PDF's depth cue is the three-component dotted number, not the type size -- ISO prints 11.9, 11.9.5 and 11.9.5.1 at the same bold weight and size, so the claim's 'same weight and size as 11.9.5' should not be treated as the evidence; (2) the claim's 'children at ###' holds only for the part of 11.9.9 on page 305 -- 11.9.9.3 Syntax rules (page 306, :13378) is a FOUR-component number also flattened to '##', so the sub-subclause children are not uniformly one level down. The flattening is a repo-wide transcription pattern rather than a 11.9-only slip: the same off-by-one appears at '## 11.7.4 General rules' (:13070), '## 11.9.6' (:13217), '## 11.9.7' (:13258), '## 11.9.10' plus all of 11.9.10.1-.4 (:13393-13428), '## 11.9.11' (:13464) and '## 11.10.4 General rules' (:13583). Fix should be a level-normalization sweep keyed on the dotted-number component count (N components -> heading level N+1 relative to the clause root), not a one-off patch of 11.9.8/11.9.9.
